html:
The Western Apache, Ndee in their own Athabaskan language, are the Apache groups of east central Arizona, in the mountains and valleys of the Mogollon Rim, the White Mountains and the Salt and Gila rivers. They include the White Mountain, Cibecue, San Carlos and Tonto groups.

Their ancestors came south from western Canada, probably between about 1300 and 1500, in the same migration as the Navajo. They farmed small fields, gathered acorns, mescal and pinyon nuts, and raided Spanish and later Mexican settlements. In the 1870s the United States put them on the Fort Apache and San Carlos reservations, and many Western Apache served as army scouts in the campaigns against Geronimo's Chiricahua. They are one of the Apache peoples, with the Lipan further east and the Yavapai to their west.
